A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and provide readable algorithms, equations, figures and complete appendices. Sections and appendix content can be matched despite the conference reformatting.

before.justification: Section 7 and Appendix A report original queueing simulations using synthetic contexts and MNIST, Heart Disease and In-Vehicle Coupon Recommendation data.

after.justification: Section 7 and Appendix A retain these original simulations and their empirical results.

M1.justification: CQB-ε and CQB-Opt retain the same exploration, optimistic selection, logistic estimation, projection and update procedures. The algorithm initialization wording changes, but the steps do not.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic queueing instances and the same three real datasets: MNIST, Heart Disease and In-Vehicle Coupon Recommendation. No evaluated task or scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Figures 2 and 4 retain the random and optimal policies, CQB-ε-Opt, CQB-TS (labeled CQB-ThS in plots), Q-UCB and Q-ThS. Their definitions in Appendix A are unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 7 and Appendix A retain the same simulation horizons, parameter settings, preprocessing, sampling procedures, arrival rates and exploration budgets. No evaluation protocol revision is documented.

E4.justification: The same sensitivity experiments vary traffic slack, server count K and context dimension d in Figures 2–3. No ablation, robustness test or supplementary empirical analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions state N = 10 instances and ±1 standard deviation across runs in Section 7. No changed run count, seed information or statistical procedure is reported; the altered Figure 4 error-bar magnitudes are result-value changes.

E6.justification: Figure 4 displays wider error bars in all three real-data panels, while retaining the mean trajectories, comparator rankings and textual findings. Figures 2–3 retain their plotted results. The uncertainty-value revisions are not explained.

T1.justification: The assumptions, mathematical definitions, regret bounds, proofs in Appendices B–F and multi-queue counterexample in Appendix G are retained. Changed references calling these items 'Theorem' do not alter their mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the contextual queueing framework, policy-switching coupling contribution, stochastic regret bound of order T^(-1/4) up to logarithmic factors, and adversarial O(log² T) bound.

C2.justification: The experimental interpretations and Appendix G discussions remain unchanged, including the algorithm-design rationale, multi-queue obstacles, slackness knowledge and preemptive policy assumptions.

D1.justification: Implementation formulas, hyperparameters and data-processing instructions are unchanged, with no new code, data-access or computing-resource information. Appendix H discloses manuscript editing rather than an experimental implementation detail.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to queueing bandits, logistic bandits, queueing reinforcement learning and nonpreemptive scheduling are unchanged. Bibliographic differences are formatting changes.

P1.justification: v2 adds acknowledgements, expanded author affiliations and Appendix H's LLM-use disclosure while retaining the core prose and section order. Numerous cross-references incorrectly replace Assumption, Lemma, Proposition or Remark with Theorem.

P2.justification: The manuscript and appendices undergo a document-wide conversion to the ICLR layout, changing the title and author block, running headers, margins, heading typography, spacing, equation wrapping and figure scaling. The four figures retain their panel organization.

improvement.justification: The scientific contributions remain unchanged. Added funding and LLM-use disclosures improve transparency, but new incorrect Theorem cross-references reduce clarity. Figure 4's wider error bars are unexplained under the unchanged statistical convention, so the PDFs do not establish whether this revision corrects an error. A reliable net quality judgment is therefore unresolved.
